season_context.local_season_notes: Cool, damp winter means outerwear, knits and suede-type textures drive sales through Q1. Retail focus moves to Christmas party and gifting from November, then January sales, with SS27 product landing from February-March and London Fashion Week AW27 in February.

sources.title: Woman & Home: autumn/winter fashion colour trends 2026
Hello! Fashion: London Fashion Week SS27 trend report
Who What Wear: London Fashion Week trends SS27

trends.name: Berry and wine shades
trends.summary: Burgundy and merlot-type berry tones are a headline colour story for the cold season, positioned as easy to combine with neutrals or brighter accents.

trends.name: Chocolate brown as the new black
trends.summary: Browns from espresso to latte are being pushed as a softer replacement for black this winter; the same cocoa shade also leads a UK kidswear trend roundup.

trends.name: Earthy greens and tomato red
trends.summary: Olive, khaki, sage and pistachio greens run alongside a punchy tomato red that was spotted in all four fashion capitals, worn either as an accent or head to toe.

trends.name: Suede beyond boots
trends.summary: Real and faux suede remain a core autumn texture after last year's surge, now moving into dresses as well as jackets and boots, often mixed with leather, knit or velvet.

trends.name: Peplums and hourglass shaping
trends.summary: London's AW26 catwalks favoured nipped waists, flared peplums and fishtail skirts with a 1950s feel, including a more fitted Burberry trench; these shapes are now reaching shops.

trends.name: Feathered eveningwear
trends.summary: Plumes on capes, corsets, jackets and stoles featured at Erdem, Chet Lo, Julien Macdonald and others in London for AW26; feather accessories offer an easier route for party season.

trends.name: Hot pink paired with black
trends.summary: Near-neon pink, frequently set against black, ran through Richard Quinn, Masha Popova and Erdem in London's AW26 shows.

trends.name: Jewel tones in velvet and cashmere for men
trends.summary: Harrods' men's guide pairs aubergine, mustard and emerald with plush velvet, fine cashmere and soft leather to lift classic winter neutrals.

trends.name: 1930s-style tailoring and the tie revival
trends.summary: Relaxed, roomier tailoring with a 1930s reference is back for men, and the necktie is reframed as a cool accessory rather than an office obligation.

trends.name: Sportswear layered over smart pieces
trends.summary: Men are mixing technical and sports pieces with tailoring, such as a windbreaker worn like a blazer or a tracksuit under an overcoat, alongside urban gorpcore outerwear.

trends.name: Embroidered menswear goes high street
trends.summary: Craft embroidery, often Indian in origin, is spreading onto men's shirts, bombers and blazers, with retailers reporting appetite for colour and pattern and embroidered shirts appearing at M&S and Zara.

trends.name: ASOS launches modest label IYAL
trends.summary: ASOS became exclusive UK and European stockist of IYAL, a fashion-led modestwear brand with occasion dresses, skirt suits, co-ord sets and matching hijabs in neutrals with coral, orange and cobalt.

trends.name: Kids: cocoa brown and burgundy
trends.summary: Children's ranges lean on milk-chocolate to deep cocoa browns, often with leopard print, plus deep burgundy for skirts, coats and mesh party dresses.

trends.name: Kids: boho lace and broderie
trends.summary: Girls' collections feature romantic broderie anglaise and lace in blush and ivory, with floaty layered dresses.

trends.name: Kids: statement collars
trends.summary: Oversized, frilled, yoked and ric-rac collars are used to freshen children's blouses, dresses and jackets.

trends.name: Kids: modern heritage checks and tweed
trends.summary: Traditional British checks, tweeds and knits are reworked into contemporary children's shapes; a UK high-street kids edit similarly leans on checkerboard trousers and stripe dungarees.

trends.name: Kids: matching co-ords
trends.summary: Two-piece sets in denim, florals and prints are offered for both girls and boys as an easy everyday look.

trends.name: Kids: cosy winter layers
trends.summary: A sponsored Next kids edit centres on borg fleece hooded jackets, knit bomber cardigans, padded colour-block coats and twill dungarees for colder months.

trends.name: Ultra-violet purple
trends.summary: Purple was the most visible colour of London's SS27 shows, seen at Erdem, Bora Aksu, Agro Studios, Ashley Williams and Geordie Campbell.

trends.name: Sheer tulle, organza and lace
trends.summary: See-through, airy layers dominated London SS27 at Simone Rocha, Susan Fang and Pauline Dujancourt; other coverage highlights tactile shine, beading and crochet.

trends.name: Sleepwear-inspired slips
trends.summary: Slip dresses, lace trims and bed jackets borrowed from nightwear appeared at Simone Rocha, Yuhan Wang and Bora Aksu, with thin straps sometimes deliberately slipping to show underlayers.

trends.name: Bold florals and clashing patterns
trends.summary: London designers including Burberry, Erdem and Chopova Lowena mixed vivid florals with stripes, pinstripes and checks rather than keeping prints separate.

trends.name: Prominent stripes
trends.summary: Preppy and nostalgic stripes became a centrepiece in London, including mismatched combinations, at Talia Byre, Burberry, Roksanda and Mithridate.

trends.name: Floral embroidery on check suiting
trends.summary: Burberry's SS27 show put embroidered mimosa and lavender sprigs on windowpane-check skirt suits and matching pumps, alongside sequin and pompom-covered skirts.

trends.name: Savile Row tailoring on the runway
trends.summary: McQueen worked with Huntsman to make bespoke-built menswear looks with long lines, broad shoulders and a high narrow waist; London SS27 reports also flag sharp tailoring as a key theme.

trends.name: Sharp pencil skirts and high-low hems
trends.summary: Slim pencil skirts, from suited to low-slung versions, plus asymmetric dipped hemlines were picked out from Mulberry, Toga, Erdem and McQueen.

trends.name: Fringe everywhere
trends.summary: Fringing moved onto bags, skirts, scarves, jackets and leather in London at Labrum, Erdem and Maximilian Raynor, echoing the same detail in New York.
